package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
)

func main() {
	type key int
	const k key = 1
	ctx := context.WithValue(context.Background(), k, 5)
	req := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/", nil).WithContext(ctx)
	fmt.Println(req.Context().Value(k).(int))
}

package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
)

func main() {
	type key int
	const k key = 1
	a := context.WithValue(context.Background(), k, 1)
	b := context.WithValue(a, k, 2)
	c := context.WithValue(b, k, 3)
	fmt.Println(c.Value(k).(int))
	fmt.Println(a.Value(k).(int))
}
Should you store Context as a long-lived struct field?
options: No. Pass it as an argument on each call

questions.text: When is an HTTP server Request.Context() canceled?
options: When the client disconnects or the request ends

questions.text: When do you take context.TODO() instead of Background()?
options: When the parent context is not clear yet

questions.text: How do you detach background work from request cancel?
Should you write your own type that implements Context?
options: Usually no: the context package functions are enough
Yes, otherwise Value does not work

questions.text: What should you do if ctx.Err() is already set before new work?
options: Do not start the work; return that error

questions.text: Why prefer AfterFunc over a goroutine on <-ctx.Done() for a short callback?
options: You can stop it before start and avoid managing an extra goroutine yourself

questions.text: How does errgroup relate to Context?
options: WithContext cancels the rest on the first error

questions.text: What does Request.Clone(ctx) do?
options: A copy of the request with that context
Nothing if ctx is already canceled

questions.text: Why are two *int pointers different WithValue keys?
options: The ints are compared by value

questions.text: If the parent is already DeadlineExceeded, what Err does a WithCancel child have?
Can you still read Value after cancel?
options: Yes. Values are independent of cancel

questions.text: Why is starting work after Done is already closed risky?
options: The work keeps using time after the request was canceled

questions.text: Do you need a custom Context to add a Value?
options: Yes, if the key is a struct

questions.text: What happens to Cause if the parent timeout fires first, then the child cancel runs?
options: The first recorded reason wins (the parent timeout)

questions.text: Request.WithContext does not mutate the original request. What does it do?
options: It returns a shallow copy with the new context

questions.text: For an outgoing HTTP client call, which context goes to NewRequestWithContext?
options: The caller context, so the request can be canceled

questions.text: Are Canceled and DeadlineExceeded distinct values under ==?
options: Yes. They are different sentinel errors

questions.text: Why must fire-and-forget work after a handler not use Request.Context()?
options: Context cannot be passed into a goroutine
The request context is canceled when the handler returns

questions.text: What about a second AfterFunc stop after a successful first?
options: false: the callback is no longer pending

questions.text: Storing Context as a long-lived struct field is an anti-pattern.
Request.Context() stays live long after the HTTP handler returns.
WithoutCancel is a way to detach work from request cancellation.
A custom Context type is usually unnecessary.
You may start new work even if ctx.Err() is already set.
Value remains readable after cancel.
Clone attaches the new context to the copy, not the original request.
errgroup.WithContext cancels the group on the first error.
Background() is a normal root in main when there is no incoming ctx.
TODO() and Background() are interchangeable with no meaning difference for readers.
Two pointer keys from different new(int) do not collide.
A WithCancel child of an already expired parent gets Canceled, not DeadlineExceeded.
An AfterFunc callback can be stopped before it starts running.
http.Request.WithContext mutates the receiver in place.
An outgoing client context should be able to cancel RoundTrip.
Canceled and DeadlineExceeded are the same sentinel.
The first recorded Cause is not overwritten by a later child cancel.
A timeout of 0 yields DeadlineExceeded immediately.
You must implement Context yourself to use WithValue.
Done can be received from again: the channel is already closed.
Where does Context belong: a long-lived field or an argument?
questions.answer: As an argument of each call.
